newsitem.title: USA: Beverly to sell Medview unit to Value Health.
newsitem.headline: Beverly to sell Medview unit to Value Health.

text.p: Beverly Enterprises Inc. said Wednesday it will sell its MedView Services business unit to Value Health Inc.

The companies have signed a definitive agreement covering the $87.5 million cash transaction, and the sale is expected to close during the fourth quarter of 1996, pending routine review by regulatory agencies. Beverly will use the proceeds from the sale to increase shareholder value by repaying debt, repurchasing stock and/or acquiring selective strategic assets that complement its core businesses.
The company said the sale of MedView will not have a material effect on Beverly's fourth quarter pretax income from ongoing operations, which is expected to meet management's internal profit plan.

On a cash flow basis, the sale will generate net proceeds totaling about $70 million. For financial reporting purposes, the sale will accelerate the recognition of future tax expenses that had been realized as non-tax deductible goodwill as a result of Beverly's June 1995 purchase of MedView. Beverly will recognize this tax expense in total during the fourth quarter of 1996.
This one-time increase in the tax provision will reduce net income by about $22 million, or $0.22 a share, but will be accretive in 1997 and beyond.

"MedView is a profitable operation and generates annual revenues of $45-$50 million, but it simply does not represent a good long-term strategic fit with Beverly's principal businesses," said David Banks, Beverly chairman and chief executive.

"We believe we can create more value for our shareholders by selling this non-strategic asset and using the $70 million net proceeds for debt repayment, stock repurchase or strategic investment in our core businesses. Simply repaying debt, for example, could add about $0.02 per share annually to Beverly's earnings beginning in 1997."

MedView provides a full range of managed care services to the workers' compensation market and is the nation's largest workers' compensation-related Preferred Provider Organization, with 120,000 member providers. It also offers case management and injury reporting/tracking services.
Beverly acquired MedView as an adjunct to its purchase of Pharmacy Management Services, Inc, in a stock purchase transaction valued at about $152 million.

PMSI is the nation's largest specialty mail-service pharmacy, serving 45,000 workers' compensation patients nationwide, and was the third major acquisition Beverly made as part of a significant expansion of its institutional pharmacy operations, Pharmacy Corporation of America.

"PMSI has proven to be a great strategic complement to our institutional pharmacy operations and will generate about $90 million in revenues for 1996," Banks said. "Considering the MedView sale, the effective net price we paid for PMSI's core mail-service business is only 70 percent of its revenues, and less than four times its projected operating income this year."
